entries.definition: A shop where you buy medicine and sometimes get simple health advice.
entries.example: The pharmacy is next to the station.

entries.definition: A doctor who looks after teeth.
entries.example: I see the dentist twice a year.

entries.definition: A planned time to see a doctor, dentist, or similar professional.
entries.example: My appointment is at three.

entries.definition: A sudden serious situation that needs help at once.
entries.example: Call this number in an emergency.

entries.definition: A special vehicle that takes very sick or hurt people to hospital.
entries.example: An ambulance came in five minutes.

entries.definition: A strip of cloth or material used to cover a cut.
entries.example: The nurse puts a bandage on my hand.

entries.definition: Physical activity you do to stay healthy and strong.
entries.example: Walking is good exercise.

entries.definition: To stop activity so your body can recover.
entries.example: Rest today and drink water.

entries.definition: A small solid piece of medicine that you swallow.
entries.example: Take one pill after dinner.

entries.definition: An illness caused by germs growing in the body.
entries.example: The cut may get an infection if it stays dirty.

entries.definition: Harm to the body, often from a fall or an accident.
entries.example: The injury is not serious.

entries.definition: Feeling that you might fall because your head seems to spin.
entries.example: I feel dizzy when I stand up fast.

entries.definition: Lacking strength in your body.
entries.example: I am weak after the fever.

entries.definition: To become healthy again after illness or injury.
entries.example: She will recover in a few days.

entries.definition: A person who is receiving care from a doctor or nurse.
entries.example: The patient waits in a quiet room.

entries.definition: A soft medicine you put on your skin.
entries.example: Use this cream on the dry skin.

entries.definition: To lose blood from a cut or from inside the body.
entries.example: My finger will bleed if I do not cover it.

entries.definition: To take air into your body and let it out.
entries.example: Breathe slowly if you feel dizzy.

entries.definition: To arrange a time to see a doctor or dentist.
entries.example: I need to make an appointment for my tooth.

entries.definition: A question you ask when someone has been ill.
entries.example: How are you feeling after the fever?

entries.definition: A kind wish for a person who is ill.
entries.example: Get well soon. We will save you a seat.

entries.definition: Used to explain which movement or action causes pain.
entries.example: It hurts when I walk on this foot.

entries.definition: The British way to say you are at the shop that sells medicine.
entries.example: I bought the cream at the chemist's this morning.

entries.definition: A nose that drips liquid, common with a cold.
entries.example: I have a runny nose and a sore throat.

entries.definition: The force of blood moving through your body, checked by a doctor.
entries.example: The nurse checks my blood pressure.

entries.definition: Simple medical help you give before a doctor arrives.
entries.example: We learn first aid at the community center.

entries.definition: Time away from work or school because you are ill.
entries.example: She is on sick leave until Monday.

entries.definition: Feeling slightly ill, not seriously sick but not well either.
entries.example: I am under the weather, so I will skip the run.

entries.definition: Getting better after an illness or injury.
entries.example: He is on the mend and can eat normally again.
